channels.regime: Oil disinflation reduces the immediate inflation impulse, but Fed policy remains restrictive and further tightening is live.
Long-end pressure eased below 5%, but the front end and dollar remain firm; conditions are less hostile, not easy.
Bank underperformance and elevated private-credit redemption queues keep weak-end transmission risk active.
AI demand/semiconductor leadership remains strong; funded contracted capex still clears the quality filter.
WTI below $90 and Saudi bypass restart show rapid crude-risk-premium unwind.
Structural diesel/jet tightness remains credible; same-session crack confirmation is still required before calling normalization.
Route normalization reduces acute scarcity urgency while structural US LNG diversification remains.
Nasdaq record and semiconductor leadership confirm strong but selective risk appetite.
Lower long yields help, but firm DXY/restrictive Fed offset the tactical metals case.
AI debt spread premium keeps financing quality a first-order filter despite equity strength.
Domestic repair remains incomplete; China matters mainly through US trade/AI and commodity transmission in this cut.
Structural supply-security theme remains strong, but a firmer dollar is a tactical headwind to metal beta.
AI semiconductor leadership reinforces the memory/HBM branch; creator short claims remain challenger evidence only.
Interconnection, self-supply, water, permitting and financing remain first-order capacity gates.

notes: Forward-looking base case: firm/range-bound DXY and sticky front-end rates despite lower WTI/10Y; this is disinflationary relief, not broad monetary easing.
Do not read Nasdaq strength as easy financial conditions: AI-linked credit remains wider and banks are underperforming.
Energy lens is now physical-vs-financial: WTI is de-escalating faster than diesel/product scarcity has been proven to normalize.
Open a dedicated banks/private-credit transmission check; do not label it systemic stress without breadth, spread and funding confirmation.
US flash PMI at 09:45 ET is the immediate invalidation/confirmation event for the dollar-rates-duration view.
Creator/social inputs remain zero-weight until independently verified.

forwardView.baseCase: DXY stays firm-to-sideways rather than collapsing; the 2Y remains sticky while lower oil caps the 10Y near/below 5%. NDX/AI can continue to outperform tactically, but broad risk-on needs banks, small caps and credit to confirm.
forwardView.dollar: Base case: firm/range-bound around the 100 area with upside pressure if PMI growth/prices beat. A durable dollar downside turn requires weaker activity/prices plus lower front-end/real yields, not crude relief alone.
forwardView.rates: Base case: curve remains relatively flat as oil relief caps the long end but Fed hawkishness keeps the front end elevated. A strong PMI/prices print can send the 10Y back toward/through 5%.
forwardView.equities: AI/semiconductors retain tactical leadership while 10Y stays contained. Treat Nasdaq strength as selective until XLF/KRE/IWM and credit participate.
forwardView.energy: Crude scarcity premium is unwinding quickly; refined products, freight and inventories now carry more information than WTI direction alone.
forwardView.gold: Mixed: lower long yields help, but a firm DXY and hawkish Fed cap tactical upside. Gold improves if real yields and DXY fall together.
forwardView.nextCatalyst: US September flash PMI, 09:45 ET Sep 23; then EIA product/inventory data.
